contract: A real SIGKILL leaves private staging until retry; locked writers, unprovable folders and a copy of a real leftover stay, dead staging is removed and named, each printed step works, and competing retries preserve exact extraction bytes.
A mixed Desktop moves ordinary groups, preserves private records, and undoes exactly.
Agent mappings move only eligible files, require journaling, and undo exactly.
Document reference surfaces stay protected while unrelated files remain movable and recoverable.
Project roots and referenced assets remain protected while nearby loose files can be organized.
Explicitly allowed synthetic sync locations have an honest apply result.
Apple metadata sidecars remain hidden while ordinary files retain their bytes.
A case-folded destination collision refuses before moving either source.
Known sync paths and Library precedence are recognized without claiming cloud hydration.
Packages stay opaque at every supported scan depth.
Hidden placeholder-shaped files remain untouched beside sortable files.
Unicode-equivalent destination names refuse without losing either distinct source.
Recent, future, and in-flight files remain held according to grace and deadline rules.
Separate roots can apply concurrently without crossing journals or names.
Graceful interruption leaves a recoverable operation at witnessed progress points.
Supplied keys seal journals and unreadable newer history blocks unsafe selection.
Truncated journals refuse or recover without changing unrecorded files.
Killed stash and pop operations resume to the exact original tree without loss or duplicates.
A killed undo resumes to the exact original tree.
Concurrent applies on one root leave an honest, loss-free, exactly recoverable state.
A killed apply leaves every file recoverable without duplication or loss.
Exact multi-parent selections refuse overlaps, preserve unselected siblings and restore original parents without source-path disclosure.
A witnessed source deletion fails honestly and preserves every survivor.
A witnessed destination intruder is never overwritten.
A witnessed source symlink swap never reads, writes, or deletes outside data.
A file written during apply retains its complete final payload.
A file occupying a destination directory prevents a destructive apply.
A witnessed permission change leaves a recoverable, honest result.
The item cap accepts its boundary and refuses the next item without mutation.
Depth limits include only intended paths and preserve the rest.
A 10k camera fixture preserves exact integrity while recording timing.
Large sparse and zero-byte files move and undo without data change.
Mixed recognized families form bounded, distinct destination groups.
Long paths remain intact and unreadable subtrees are disclosed.
Hostile filenames survive plan, apply, and undo without reinterpretation.
Legal case-distinct paths apply safely on a case-sensitive volume.
Cross-device copying preserves content, mtime, and recoverability.
Cross-volume moves preserve data through ordinary and interrupted copy paths.
Same-device exFAT fallback moves files without loss.
Full-volume apply remains honest and recoverable.
Read-only volumes plan but refuse apply without mutation.
Low descriptor limits fail honestly without silently dropping journaling.
An unwritable journal state directory prevents an unjournaled apply.
A partial undo persists progress and resumes after a volume hazard.
Sweep decides by name and does not block on a FIFO; hostile archive members refuse safely.
A killed apply reads back as interrupted with true counts, an unknown operation id is named as such, a contended apply says whether to wait, and status names no file.

A plan written by sweep propose moves only the files it names; an apply killed part-way is reported as interrupted and undo restores every original path and byte, with skipped, unnamed and never-eligible files untouched throughout.
Ordinary archive listing and extraction preserve exact paths and bytes.
Killed unpack never publishes a partial target and retry extracts the exact archive.
Captured archive quarantine is preserved and exactly read back before publication, including AppleDouble storage.
The scenario wrapper propagates failure, signal, and completion status.

A tagged item is left alone and counted without its name, --include-tagged is loud and keeps the tag through move and undo, Finder comments are not read, and an item tagged after planning is not moved.
stash clears tagged items too, keeps their tags through stash and pop, and reports the folder clear only when nothing was left behind.
unpack extracts a small archive made in the scenario to its exact bytes after etude-core changes.
A tagged item whose move would cross volumes stays in place with its tag and is counted by name, in sweep and in stash, while untagged items still cross.

sweep --scheme tags plans and exports a tag plan that writes nothing, lists each tag with its file count and marks new ones, applies only from the exported plan, adds tags after the ones a file has and moves nothing, undoes to the exact previous bytes, leaves a file whose tags changed since apply, skips a file whose tags cannot be read, and refuses a stale plan.
A tag apply killed part-way is reported as interrupted with true counts and repeated undo restores every file's exact previous tag bytes, with personal, hidden and linked files never tagged.
After sweep adds tags, stash holds and pops the folder with those tags intact, sweep undo still restores the earlier tags, and unpack extracts a synthetic archive to its exact bytes.
Sweep undo retains a folder needed by a live stash; pop and repeated undo restore every original path and byte, and unpack extracts exact archive bytes.
A forged personal member refuses despite a recomputed plan digest, ordinary sweep applies and undoes, stash restores its file, and unpack preserves archive bytes.
A failed journal append stops before the next move, undo restores the durable prefix plus one in-flight entry, stash round-trips and unpack preserves history.
A 5,000-file tar extracts completely on every run while the size check races the renames macOS tar makes.
SIGKILL during zip, tar and tar.gz extraction leaves no archive copy in the temporary folder.
Many unpack runs at the same time each extract a safe zip, so one run never refuses because another run is using the same descriptor number.
A mistyped flag moves nothing, help answers from any position, a printed next command acts on the files shown, and a pop with two batches names both.

Existing-folder routes preserve safety holds, require valid destinations and profiles, count in-place files, move two routed files with no three-file floor and undo them, and bind exported plans to profile bytes.
Opaque item ids restore exactly one held item, reject unknown items, report the remaining held count, and restore all remaining bytes.
Sweep apply emits versioned stderr progress with exact durable counts and one JSON stdout envelope; undo reports durable reversals the same way; unsupported commands refuse the flag.
A folder or archive the tool may not read gets an error that names it and the next step, and is never reported as clear or as having no work.

A failure says whether anything moved and prints only steps that work and touch only that work; extra words, repeated flags, a mistyped group, a bad journal key and the home folder each get a refusal that changes nothing.

Every sweep failure, and each plan and scan failure sweep and stash share, states the real cause, a next step that works and the code that fits, in plain words and without a panic; an undo that leaves a file behind is incomplete and exits non-zero.

Every remaining stash failure names what failed, whether anything moved and a next step that works, in plain words and without a panic; a pop that leaves an item behind is incomplete and exits non-zero, and printed steps work when followed.

Every unpack failure names what failed, whether anything was left and a next step that works, in plain words and without a panic: damaged, empty and password-protected archives, unsupported names and downloads in progress, size limits, full disks, options in either order, and leftover folders. Unsafe archives stay refused, and printed steps work when followed.

One condition gets one answer across the tools: a missing folder reads the same on every command and counts agree with their nouns. A failed undo or pop says only what is true, and its printed steps work when followed. A scan does not offer an apply it knows will refuse, and a relative archive gets the same free-space floor as an absolute one.

sweep undo --id reverses exactly one apply and opens only that record, so one record that will not open cannot block the others. The refusal for such a record lists the records that do open, newest first, each with a step that works, and changes none of them. Undoing an older apply before a newer one never overwrites a file or puts one in the wrong place: it restores, or stops and says so, and a wrong key loses nothing.

A file or folder with the immutable flag is held and counted by sweep and stash, never moved or tagged; an item locked after planning is held at move time, a locked destination folder refuses before any move, undo and pop restore only what moved, and unpack extracts beside a locked file.
Every tool's progress records match the filesystem on complete runs, and a kill leaves whole records, no terminal record and no overstated count.

An argument that is not valid UTF-8 never panics sweep, stash or unpack: as a path or a flag value, in text and --json, the tool exits 2 with reason invalid_arguments, says nothing was changed, names the argument with the bad bytes shown as ?, and prints no raw invalid or control byte. A valid non-ASCII argument still works.

sweep files into an existing folder it may write but not list and undoes it, a destination that links outside the root is refused with nothing landing outside, stash holds and pops, and unpack extracts to the exact bytes.
A sweep apply paused part way, confirmed stopped and killed is brought fully home by undo with every byte intact; a 600-file stash and pop round-trips; unpack extracts to the exact bytes.

A scan holds no key, prunes nothing and, with no key supplied, reads no key material. A stash whose undo record is over 30 days old keeps that record through a sweep apply, which drops an old sweep record it can open before it moves and keeps its own; pop brings every file back with its bytes, and the popped record expires once 30 days old. An old sweep record under another key survives an apply under that key and a wrong-key undo, and the right key then undoes it with every byte. unpack extracts a small zip to its bytes.
A failed cross-volume move onto a nearly full disk image preserves source bytes and leaves no destination copy; sweep apply and undo, stash and pop, and unpack also round-trip exact bytes.

A folder, extension or duration the person typed is shown as typed, with no debug quotes or backslash escapes and with control characters shown as ?: sweep and stash refuse with exit 2 and the exact text, nothing moved. Stash and pop and an unpack round trip still work in a folder named with a quote and a space.

Under --scheme existing a saved route's missing folder is listed in the plan, created only when files move into it and removed by undo once empty, with every byte intact; a route with no files creates nothing; one or two routed files move into the created folder, are never reported as having no group and come back on undo with the folder removed; one or two PDFs move into a Documents folder that is already here and undo keeps it, while two with no Documents folder stay and the plan says why; a file holding the route name refuses with profile_invalid and moves nothing; a stash and pop round-trips and unpack extracts exact bytes.

Routing hints work as printed without file or found folder names; saving validated routes is private, conflict-free, complete-apply-only, keeps the person's text, ignores stale pending files, reports a failed save after moves against the profile with a working step, and invalidates older profile-bound plans. The hint is a short sentence with the command on its own line, the folder shown as typed. Stash and unpack contracts still match their pinned files and sweep's shared reason rules, and each refuses an unknown option with the envelope its contract describes.

A sweep apply paused part way, confirmed stopped, with its source folder swapped for a link to an outside folder holding the same names, refuses with plan_stale, names the folder, takes nothing from outside and leaves the pending file in the real folder; with the folder put back, undo brings every file home with its bytes; a stash and pop round-trips and unpack extracts exact bytes.

unpack declaration 9 lists private_copy_unopened once, retry later, subject input, for extract and list; sweep and stash do not list it; a damaged zip is still archive_unreadable with exit 3 and leaves no folder; unpack extracts a safe zip with exact bytes, sweep plans a folder, and a stash and pop round-trips.

Two applies of one folder, made one after the other with no wait and no timing, are both reversible. The first sweep undo exits 0 and says after the Restored line that another apply of this folder can still be undone, with a step that works when run exactly as printed, for folder names with a space, a single quote and a tab; the second says nothing more, and the folder then equals the original. sweep undo --json gives details.remaining_reversible 1 then 0 and records_not_opened 0, and sweep undo with no folder says the same for the folder it undid. A name with a byte that is not UTF-8 is unproven where the filesystem refuses it.

The lines under a sweep plan say what each step does: the in-use line is printed once before the steps, Review and Apply say they scan again, Save offers ~/sweep.plan, then ~/sweep-2.plan when the first is taken, and a scan of the home folder offers a file outside it. A plan made before the folder changed is refused with exit 2 and moves nothing, and its step to remake the plan keeps --inspect-content and the --map route that was used and tells the person to add routes that matched no file.
